name: Janette H. Malata-Silva
half:
Janette H. Malata-Silva has advised three theses in this repository, with supervision activity spanning from 2021 to 2023. No advisees are recorded for 2026, indicating a pause in recent supervision within this specific dataset. The adviser’s portfolio demonstrates a focus on educational development, particularly in language instruction and community engagement. Their supervised work covers sub-topics including language and literacy, which appears in two items, as well as teacher training, communication studies, instructional design, community development, and arts and creative practice, each appearing once. This distribution suggests a versatility in guiding research that bridges pedagogical theory with practical application in diverse educational contexts.

One notable thesis from 2023, titled "Designing a Training Framework for Filipino Teachers Using Communicative Language Teaching Activities in Teaching Oral Conversation Fluency to EFL Chinese Adult Students," explores the professional development needs of Filipino online English teachers. This study highlights gaps in Online Language Teacher Education and addresses specific challenges faced by educators serving Chinese adult students. Another thesis from 2022, "Contextualization of Grade 3 Instructional Materials; Basis for a Design of Bulacan Tagalog-Based Science Materials," focuses on instructional design within the framework of Mother Tongue-Based Multilingual Education. This qualitative study investigates the creation of science materials using Bulacan-Tagalog for public school students. The earliest recorded thesis from 2021, "Enhancing Selected Literacy Programs of a University Volunteer Service Program Through Outcomes-Based Education," examines the integration of Outcomes-Based Education to improve literacy initiatives managed by a university volunteer service program. These examples illustrate a consistent interest in improving educational outcomes through structured training, contextualized materials, and program evaluation. The adviser appears to support research that is both theoretically grounded and practically oriented toward solving specific educational challenges in language and literacy.

The research was driven by the mandate for Mother Tongue-Based Multilingual Education (MTB-MLE), addressing the need for localized educational resources. Tags associated with this work include baliwag, bulacan tagalog, public school, and science instructional material, pointing to a strong interest in regional linguistic adaptation within the public school system.

This work intersects language and literacy with community development and arts and creative practice. It explores how integrating Outcomes-Based Education (OBE) can improve the effectiveness of literacy initiatives managed by the UPLB Ugnayan ng Pahinungod. The study is situated against a backdrop of global learning poverty and specific challenges faced by volunteer service programs. Tags for this thesis include literacy program, multi case research design, outcome based education, and university volunteer service program.
